headline: Regulatory state is increasingly read out and predicted at cell-type resolution across modalities
label: Cell Type Resolved Regulatory Profiling
summary: Preprints pair cell-type-conditioned prediction with single-cell, long-read and multi-omic readouts, tying regulatory state to cell identity in tissues and disease.
synthesis: The dominant thread is resolving regulatory state by cell type, with both predictive and experimental routes. AlphaGenome 2 predicts cell-type-conditioned regulatory activity and variant effects from 1-Mb DNA and provides an enhancer-gene link atlas. Experimental methods add measurement: TrES-seq pairs scRNA-seq with nanobody-Tn5 histone mark profiling, COMET assigns bulk long reads to cell types by methylation, and Superb-seq links Cas9 edits to single-cell transcriptomes. DRAFT infers dynamic regulatory networks from time-resolved multi-omics trajectories, and a pan-cancer lncRNA atlas links lncRNAs to regulons. Siphon-seq and the heart isoform atlas extend this to purity-aware platelet profiling and full-length isoforms. What is new is the coupling of perturbation, epigenomic or isoform readouts to cell identity; these data could in principle test cell-type-conditioned predictors, though no item does so directly.
